1	# kolosok-rehack — AI Development Guidelines
2	
3	Team **Kolosok** at the **European Hackathon League (EHL) Grand Finale**, Munich (TUM.ai).
4	This file is the rulebook for every AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) and human working in this repo.
5	**Read it fully before your first change.** Human setup (GitHub token, credentials) lives in `README-Human`.
6	
7	Source: [EHL Finale – All you need to know](https://tum-ai.notion.site/REDACTED)
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 0. Hard rules (non-negotiable)
12	
13	1. **Entire must be enabled and every commit must carry a checkpoint.** The organisers will reject a submission that does not use Entire. No Entire → no valid submission.
14	2. **All work goes through git and gets pushed to `origin`.** Nothing that exists only on one laptop counts.
15	3. **`main` must always be demo-able.** We have a strict 6-minute slot for pitch + demo + questions.
16	4. **Never commit secrets** (API keys, tokens, `.env`). Entire redacts secrets in session logs, but do not rely on that.
17	5. **Never rewrite pushed history** (no `push --force`, no amending/rebasing pushed commits, no deleting `entire/*` branches or refs). Checkpoints are tied to commits; rewriting history can orphan them.
18	
19	## 1. Key times (Munich local time)
20	
21	| When | What |
22	|---|---|
23	| Sat 10 Oct, 11:00–11:30 | Entire technical onboarding |
24	| **Sat 10 Oct, 13:00** | **Challenge selection deadline** (captain, on https://ehl.gg/) |
25	| Sat 13:30 → Sun 12:00 | Hacking |
26	| **Sun 11 Oct, 12:00** | **Submission deadline** — hard stop |
27	| Sun 12:00–14:30 | Challenge pitches (6 min incl. Q&A) |
28	| Sun 15:30–16:30 | Main-stage final (6 teams) |
29	
30	Internal targets: **feature freeze Sun 10:00**, first full submission by **Sun 10:30**, final re-submission by **11:45**.
31	Submissions can be repeated as often as we like before the deadline, so submit early and update.
32	
33	**Challenge:** BMW Group — AI for Product Decision Making: an app that turns customer feedback, product/sales data and web research into prioritized, PM-reviewed customer requirements with a full audit trail. Details: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md).
34	
35	## 2. Setup checklist (each machine, once)
36	
37	Prerequisites: `git` on `PATH` (Entire shells out to it — it fails with `exec: "git": executable file not found` otherwise).
38	
39	```bash
40	# 1. Install Entire (bash / Git Bash). On Windows the binary ends up in ~/.local/bin/entire.exe
41	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
42	
43	# 2. On the main branch of this repo:
44	git checkout main && git pull
45	git config pull.rebase true      # plain `git pull` makes merge commits, which carry no checkpoint
46	entire login                     # if not logged in yet
47	entire enable                    # enables session tracking in this repo
48	entire agent add claude-code     # install hooks for your agent; `entire agent list` shows others (codex, cursor, …)
49	
50	# 3. Verify
51	entire status
52	entire doctor                    # if anything looks off
53	```
54	
55	**You are set up correctly when** your next commit prints:
56	
57	```
58	[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done
59	```
60	
61	If you don't see that line, stop and fix Entire before writing more code.
62	
63	## 3. Git workflow
64	
65	- **Commit small and often** — at least every meaningful step, ideally every 15–30 min of agent work. Each commit becomes a checkpoint linking the code to the prompt/reasoning behind it.
66	- **Commit only from within a tracked agent session**, after the agent made the change with its file-edit tools. Hand-made commits, merge commits and shell (`sed`, `echo >`) edits get no checkpoint.
67	- **After every commit** check the checkpoint is there: `git log -1 --format=%B` must show an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line. If it is missing, fix it *before* pushing.
68	- **Commit messages:** imperative, prefixed by area, e.g. `feat(api): add route planner endpoint`, `fix(ui): handle empty results`, `docs: update run instructions`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `demo`.
69	- **Sync before push:** `git pull --rebase` on *unpushed* local commits only, then `git push`. Resolve conflicts, never discard teammates' work.
70	- **Branches:** short-lived feature branches (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`) merged back to `main` quickly (within a few hours). Trivial fixes may go straight to `main`. Do not let branches drift overnight.
71	- **Do not commit:** `.env`, credentials, `node_modules/`, virtualenvs, large datasets or model weights, build artifacts. Add them to `.gitignore` as soon as they appear.
72	- **After every push** check the `[entire] Pushing … checkpoint ref(s)` line appeared.
73	
74	## 4. How agents should work here
75	
76	**Before starting a task**
77	1. Read this README, `README-Human` and **`VISION.md`** (our product idea, shared context for everyone); look at `Concept/` for the architecture sketch (`root.drawio`).
78	2. `git pull` and check what others (human or agent) are doing:
79	   - `entire recap` — summary of recent checkpoint activity
80	   - `entire session list` — active/past agent sessions
81	   - `entire checkpoint search "<topic>"` — has someone already tried this?
82	3. Confirm the task is not already in progress to avoid duplicate work.
83	
84	**While working**
85	- Keep scope tight: do the requested task, nothing more. Hackathon time is the scarcest resource.
86	- Prefer simple, working solutions over clever ones; a reliable demo beats extra features.
87	- Match existing structure, naming, and style. Don't introduce new frameworks or languages without team agreement.
88	- Keep the app runnable at every commit. If you break `main`, fixing it is the top priority.
89	- Document how to run anything you add (see §6) in the same commit.
90	- Use `entire agent-help` for machine-readable, version-accurate CLI usage instead of guessing commands.
91	
92	**Handing off / resuming**
93	- Use `entire session resume <branch>` or `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>` to pick up someone else's context instead of re-deriving it.
94	- `entire dispatch` produces a summary of recent agent work — use it for handoffs and pitch prep.
95	
96	**When unsure** about requirements or the challenge brief: ask the team; challenge questions go to the partners on **Discord** (https://discord.gg/4UDNd5TAg). Do not assume partner support is available overnight.
97	
98	## 5. LLMs, keys, and resources
99	
100	- **OpenAI** is a tech partner: each participant has **75 USD** of LLM/API credits. Use them for app-level LLM calls.
101	- Keys go in a local `.env` (gitignored) and are read via environment variables; provide a `.env.example` with placeholder names only.
102	- Be mindful of token spend; `entire session tokens <id>` / `entire checkpoint tokens <id>` show usage.
103	
104	## 6. Demo & submission readiness
105	
106	- Judging is a **strict 6-minute slot including questions** — design the product around one clear, rehearsable demo flow.
107	- Keep a **"How to run"** section here up to date (install, env vars, start command, demo script).
108	- Before submission: everything pushed, Entire checkpoints present (`entire checkpoint list`), all relevant content uploaded on https://ehl.gg/.
109	- Have a fallback (recorded video or screenshots) in case the live demo fails.
110	
111	### How to run
112	
113	Decision graph API (Phase 1 — Postgres + the `add_node` core + the 8 agent tools from `VISION.md`):
114	
115	```bash
116	docker compose up -d                 # Postgres on localhost:5432
117	cd backend
118	python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate   # (or `source .venv/bin/activate` on Linux/macOS)
119	pip install -r requirements.txt
120	python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000   # creates tables on startup
121	```
122	
123	Run tests (needs the Postgres container up): `cd backend && pytest`.
124	
125	API docs once running: http://localhost:8000/docs. Endpoints: `GET /nodes`, `GET /nodes/{id}`, `GET /nodes/{id}/inputs`, `GET /nodes/{id}/dependents`, `POST /tools/{import_source,query_data,web_search,add_claim,add_assumption,propose_requirement,score,challenge,ask_pm}`, `POST /decide` (PM only). This is the data-transit contract for the GUI, agent-loop and ingestion modules.
126	
127	### Agent loop (concept + runnable skeleton)
128	
129	`agent-loop/README.md` has the design for the Look → Decide → Act → Pause loop from `VISION.md`.
130	`agent-loop/loop.py` is a thin, runnable skeleton of it: `decide()` is a stubbed rule-based
131	placeholder (clearly marked) for where a real LLM call goes; the rest already talks to the
132	real API. Run it with the backend up:
133	
134	```bash
135	cd agent-loop
136	python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate
137	pip install -r requirements.txt
138	python loop.py          # or: pytest (tests decide()'s logic without a server)
139	```
140	
141	### For teammates building GUI / agent-loop / ingestion
142	
143	Build against the HTTP API above, not against `backend/app/` directly — it's the one shared contract, so all three modules can be developed independently without colliding on the same Python code.
144	
145	- **Base URL:** `http://localhost:8000` once the steps above are running. CORS is open (`allow_origins=["*"]`), so a browser-based GUI can call it directly.
146	- **Every write goes through one of the `/tools/*` endpoints or `/decide`** — there is no other way to write to the graph, by design (see `VISION.md` → "Write rules").
147	- **Errors:** `400` with a `{"detail": "..."}` body means a rule was rejected (missing required input, input id doesn't exist, non-PM caller on `/decide`). `404` means a `GET` asked for a node id that doesn't exist. Anything else is a bug — report it.
148	- **Node types, edge relations, and which tool writes what** are specified in `VISION.md` → "Data model" and "Agent tools"; the API enforces those rules server-side, so you don't need to re-check them client-side.
149	- **Example** (turn evidence into a claim):
150	  ```bash
151	  curl -X POST localhost:8000/tools/add_claim -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
152	    -d '{"content":{"text":"seats too narrow"},"evidence_ids":["EVD-001"],"created_by":"agent:researcher"}'
153	  ```
154	- Tests in `backend/tests/test_graph.py` double as runnable examples of every tool's expected inputs/outputs.

2	why"). Needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment (see repo root .env.example).
3	"""
4	
5	import json
6	import os
7	
8	from openai import OpenAI
9	
10	MODEL = os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini")
11	
12	_CONTENT = {
13	    "type": "object",
14	    "description": "the node's content. Always a JSON object, e.g. {\"text\": \"...\"} or "
15	                   "{\"quote\": \"...\", \"url\": \"...\"} — never a plain string.",
16	    "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
17	}
18	_IDS = {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
19	_RATIONALE = {"type": "string", "description": "why this action, for the node's rationale field"}
20	
21	TOOLS = [
22	    {"type": "function", "function": {
23	        "name": "query_data", "description": "Look into the BMW files for evidence.",
24	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
25	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "source_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
26	                        "required": ["content", "source_ids", "rationale"]}}},
27	    {"type": "function", "function": {
28	        "name": "web_search", "description": "Find competitor info/trends; content must include a url.",
29	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
30	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
31	                        "required": ["content", "inputs", "rationale"]}}},
32	    {"type": "function", "function": {
33	        "name": "add_claim", "description": "State a finding, linked to its evidence.",
34	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
35	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "evidence_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
36	                        "required": ["content", "evidence_ids", "rationale"]}}},
37	    {"type": "function", "function": {
38	        "name": "add_assumption", "description": "State a forward-looking guess, clearly marked as not evidence.",
39	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
40	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
41	                        "required": ["content", "inputs", "rationale"]}}},
42	    {"type": "function", "function": {
43	        "name": "propose_requirement", "description": "Turn one or more claims into a requirement.",
44	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
45	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "claim_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
46	                        "required": ["content", "claim_ids", "rationale"]}}},
47	    {"type": "function", "function": {
48	        "name": "score", "description": "Run the fixed scoring formula on a requirement.",
49	        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
50	            "content": _CONTENT, "target_id": {"type": "string"}, "formula": {"type": "string"},
51	            "rationale": _RATIONALE},
52	            "required": ["content", "target_id", "formula", "rationale"]}}},
53	    {"type": "function", "function": {
54	        "name": "challenge", "description": "Look for counter-evidence to an existing node.",
55	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
56	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "target_id": {"type": "string"}, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
57	                        "required": ["content", "target_id", "rationale"]}}},
58	    {"type": "function", "function": {
59	        "name": "ask_pm", "description": "Stop and ask the PM a question when no good next step exists.",
60	        "parameters": {"type": "object",
61	                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
62	                        "required": ["content", "rationale"]}}},
63	]
64	
65	SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
66	    "You are the agent building a product-decision graph (VISION.md). You are given the "
67	    "current graph's signals (sources without evidence, evidence without a claim, claims "
68	    "without a requirement, stale nodes, open questions). Pick exactly one tool call that "
69	    "makes the most progress right "
70	    "now, and fill in its 'rationale' argument explaining why. If nothing useful can be done, "
71	    "call ask_pm."
72	)

74	
75	def decide_with_llm(signals: dict, client: OpenAI | None = None) -> tuple[str, dict]:
76	    client = client or OpenAI()
77	    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
78	        model=MODEL,
79	        messages=[
80	            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
81	            {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(signals, default=str)},
82	        ],
83	        tools=TOOLS,

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd


def read_csv_files():
    csv_directory = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        csv_file.stem: pd.read_csv(csv_file)
        for csv_file in csv_directory.glob("*.csv")
    }


def build_criticism_matrix(tables):
    """Count distinct defect/usability feedback IDs per vehicle part and model."""
    if not tables:
        return pd.DataFrame().rename_axis(index="Vehicle part", columns="Vehicle model")

    feedback = pd.concat(tables.values(), ignore_index=True)
    criticism = feedback.loc[
        feedback["Feedback Type"].isin(["Defect", "Difficult to Use"])
        & feedback["Vfc level2 Name"].notna()
        & feedback["Vfc level2 Name"].ne("no_class_found")
    ]
    return (
        criticism.groupby(["Vfc level2 Name", "Derivate (e-code)"])["ID"]
        .nunique()
        .unstack(fill_value=0)
        .rename_axis(index="Vehicle part", columns="Vehicle model")
    )

input.new_string:
SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
You are the agent building a product-decision graph for BMW product managers (PMs).
The graph grows along one chain: Source (a data file) -> Evidence (query_data: one concrete
finding from a source) -> Claim (add_claim) -> Requirement (propose_requirement) -> score.
Each turn you get the graph's signals and your recent_actions; pick exactly ONE tool call.

Rules:
1. Evidence must contain real data. For query_data, read the source's content in `sources`
   and put one specific finding in content: {"text": "<finding>", "quote": "<exact row
   text>", "source_ref": "<row reference>"}. Never write an instruction, plan or request
   ("inspect the file...") as evidence. If a source has no usable content, call ask_pm.
2. Never invent data. Claims summarize evidence; requirements build on claims.
3. Only use node ids that appear in the signals. Ids are never guessed.
4. Move down the chain: if evidence_without_claim is non-empty, prefer add_claim over another
   query_data; if claims_without_requirement is non-empty, prefer propose_requirement.
5. Read recent_actions. Do not repeat a finding you already recorded, do not retry a call
   that just errored with the same arguments, and do not pick the same tool a third time in
   a row unless it records a genuinely new finding.
6. Always fill 'rationale' with why this step, citing the ids it builds on.
7. If no step makes real progress, call ask_pm with a specific question.
8. If `required_action` is given, call exactly that tool with those ids and write its
   content and rationale.
"""


def decide_with_llm(
    signals: dict,
    history: list[dict] | None = None,
    forced: tuple[str, dict] | None = None,
    client: OpenAI | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """forced=(tool, ids) pins the tool and its input ids (hybrid mode); the LLM then only
    writes content + rationale."""
    client = client or OpenAI()
    payload = {"signals": signals, "recent_actions": history or []}
    tool_choice = "required"
    if forced:
        tool, ids = forced
        payload["required_action"] = {"tool": tool, **ids}
        tool_choice = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": tool}}
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(payload, default=str)},
        ],
        tools=TOOLS,
        tool_choice=tool_choice,
    )

"""Throwaway: 1 run per model x DECIDE_MODE, with token usage and quote-fidelity checks."""
import csv, json, os, subprocess, sys

REPO = r"C:\Users\Alex\HAckAI\kolosok-rehack"
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "agent-loop"))
import openai, llm, loop, seed  # noqa: E402

CSV = os.path.join(REPO, "agent-loop", "sample_data", "demo_feedback.csv")
ROW_TEXTS = {r["text_or_value"] for r in csv.DictReader(open(CSV, encoding="utf-8"))}
usage = {"in": 0, "out": 0}


class Client:
    def __init__(self, model):
        self._c, self._model = openai.OpenAI(), model
        self.chat = self
        self.completions = self

    def create(self, **kw):
        if self._model.startswith("gpt-6"):
            kw["reasoning_effort"] = "none"  # luna rejects tools otherwise
        resp = self._c.chat.completions.create(**kw)
        usage["in"] += resp.usage.prompt_tokens
        usage["out"] += resp.usage.completion_tokens
        return resp


def reset():
    subprocess.run(["docker", "compose", "exec", "-T", "db", "psql", "-q", "-U", "kolosok",
                    "-d", "decision_graph", "-c",
                    "TRUNCATE edges, nodes CASCADE; UPDATE node_counters SET next = 1;"],
                   cwd=REPO, check=True, capture_output=True)


out = []
for model in ["gpt-4o-mini", "gpt-6-luna"]:
    for mode in ["llm", "hybrid"]:
        reset()
        seed.seed(CSV)
        llm.MODEL = model
        llm.OpenAI = lambda m=model: Client(m)
        os.environ["DECIDE_MODE"] = mode
        usage.update({"in": 0, "out": 0})
        actions = []
        for r in loop.run(max_actions=8):
            c = r.get("content") or {}
            actions.append({"id": r.get("id"), "error": r.get("error"),
                            "text": c.get("text"), "quote": c.get("quote"),
                            "quote_exact": c.get("quote") in ROW_TEXTS if c.get("quote") else None,
                            "content_keys": sorted(c), "rationale": r.get("rationale")})
        nodes = loop.requests.get(f"{loop.API_BASE}/nodes").json()
        edges = {n["id"]: [i["id"] for i in loop.requests.get(
            f"{loop.API_BASE}/nodes/{n['id']}/inputs").json()] for n in nodes}
        out.append({"model": model, "mode": mode, "tokens_in": usage["in"],
                    "tokens_out": usage["out"], "actions": actions, "edges": edges})
        print(model, mode, "done", usage, flush=True)

reset()
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[1], "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

# Agent loop evaluation: 2 models × 2 decision modes

I read "1 run per tool" as one run for each combination: gpt-4o-mini and gpt-6-luna, each in `llm` mode (the model picks every step) and `hybrid` mode (fixed rules pick the step, the model writes the content). That's 4 runs on the seeded 12-row demo CSV, each starting from an empty database, with an 8-action limit. All 4 ran cleanly: no stalls, no errors, no guessed ids, and every graph link points to a real node.

| Run | Actions | Graph built | Tokens in / out | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4o-mini · llm | 8 | 3 findings → 2 claims → 2 requirements → 1 score | 21,177 / 720 | $0.0036 |
| 4o-mini · hybrid | 4 | 1 finding → 1 claim → 1 requirement → question to PM | 10,907 / 342 | $0.0018 |
| **luna · llm** | 8 | 3 findings → 3 claims → 2 requirements | 22,487 / 878 | **$0.0027** |
| luna · hybrid | 4 | 1 finding → 1 claim → 1 requirement → question to PM | 11,326 / 425 | $0.0013 |

All 4 runs together cost about $0.009. luna is roughly 25% cheaper than 4o-mini for the same work.

## What works now
- **Evidence is real data.** 7 of the 8 evidence nodes quote a CSV row exactly. The 8th (luna, hybrid) quotes the whole CSV line with the columns joined together; the content is right, just not word for word.
- **The chain moves forward on its own.** Both models in `llm` mode followed the order evidence → claim → requirement, then went back for a different row. Neither repeated a finding.

## Quality: luna is clearly better
- **luna's requirements are more specific.** For example: *"Improve … recognition of place names … and validate recognition performance with representative in-car utterances."* gpt-4o-mini wrote *"needs improvement in understanding…"* and *"There should be improved features for electric range…"*.
- **luna's rationales are better.** They cite node ids and explain why a step isn't a repeat: *"complements, but does not repeat, the long-trip planning claim CLM-002"*.
- **gpt-4o-mini overclaims and copies.** From one dealer-trend row it claimed a *"growing customer concern"*. In hybrid mode its claim was a word-for-word copy of the evidence.

## Problems found (both models)

| # | Problem | Evidence | Possible fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Scoring doesn't exist.** The score tool has no real formula behind it. | 4o-mini's score node only restates the requirement. Both hybrid runs stopped to ask the PM *"what criteria should we use for scoring?"* | Define the scoring formula. Ideally it uses the CSV's `reliability` column, which no run used. This is a backend task. |
| 2 | **No consolidation.** Every claim rests on exactly one row, so every requirement has n=1 evidence. | Rows 2, 8 and 11 are all about charging. luna saw the link but still made a separate claim. | Prompt: "if a new finding supports an existing theme, add it to that claim's evidence". Or extract all evidence first, then group it. |
| 3 | **The `quote` field gets misused.** Models put their own text in `quote` on requirements and questions, which looks like a citation but isn't. | 4o-mini hybrid: REQ-001 and QST-001 "quote" themselves. | Offer the `quote` and `source_ref` fields only on `query_data`'s content. |
| 4 | **Questions to the PM aren't linked to what they're about.** | Both QST-001 nodes have no inputs, though each asks about REQ-001. | Make the fixed rules pass the relevant ids to `ask_pm`, or let the model fill `inputs` in hybrid mode. |
| 5 | **Hybrid mode stops after one finding per file**, as documented. | 4 steps, then a question to the PM. | Only fixable by giving the rules a "more rows left" signal. |
| 6 | **Input tokens grow with the source size.** Each step's request includes about 2.7k input tokens, mostly the full CSV. | 12 rows already account for most of it; the real customer feedback would blow past the context window. | Chunking (already marked as a shortcut in the code). |

## Recommendation
**Make gpt-6-luna in `llm` mode the default.** It's cheaper and produces better requirements. To switch, `llm.py` needs `reasoning_effort="none"` when the model is luna. I passed it from the test runner only, so the shipped code can't run luna as-is.

After that, I'd fix #1 (scoring) and #2 (consolidation) first: they decide whether the result looks like real prioritized requirements or a list of single-verbatim paraphrases. #3 and #4 are small cleanups.

Want me to do the luna switch plus #3 and #4 now, and take #1 and #2 as a separate step?

This is one run per combination, so it's indicative rather than statistical. The demo data is synthetic and tidy, so the real BMW customer feedback will be harder. The test runner stays in the scratchpad, nothing in the repo changed, and the database has been reset.
Update the feature readme with problems, Ill hand it to the teammate

54	
55	Early live runs (gpt-4o-mini, then gpt-6-luna: 1 of 3 clean) kept calling `query_data` and
56	never reached a claim. Causes: the seeded Source held only a filename, so evidence was the
57	model's own "inspect the file" request and it rightly refused to build claims on it; Decide had
58	no memory of its last actions; and once a source had evidence it vanished from the signals,
59	so the model guessed ids. Fixed by real rows in Sources (`seed.py`), the `sources` signal plus
60	`inputs` on each evidence node, recent-action history, and a stricter prompt. Live result after
61	the fix: 8/8 actions without errors, Source → Evidence → Claim → Requirement → Score, then the
62	next finding.

## Evaluation (2026-10-11) — 1 run per model × mode

Setup: fresh DB, `seed.py sample_data/demo_feedback.csv`, `run(max_actions=8)`.

| Model · mode | Actions | Graph built | Tokens in / out | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-4o-mini · llm | 8 | 3 EVD → 2 CLM → 2 REQ → 1 SCR | 21,177 / 720 | $0.0036 |
| gpt-4o-mini · hybrid | 4 | 1 EVD → 1 CLM → 1 REQ → QST | 10,907 / 342 | $0.0018 |
| **gpt-6-luna · llm** | 8 | 3 EVD → 3 CLM → 2 REQ | 22,487 / 878 | **$0.0027** |
| gpt-6-luna · hybrid | 4 | 1 EVD → 1 CLM → 1 REQ → QST | 11,326 / 425 | $0.0013 |

Prices: gpt-6-luna $0.10 / $0.50 per M tokens in/out, gpt-4o-mini $0.15 / $0.60 (third-party
listings — check OpenAI's pricing page). One run each, so indicative, not statistical.

What works: no stalls, 0 errors and 0 guessed ids in 24 actions; 7/8 evidence quotes match a
CSV row exactly; both models walk the chain unprompted and pick a new row each time.

Quality: **gpt-6-luna is clearly better** — testable requirements ("…validate recognition
performance with representative in-car utterances") and rationales that cite ids. gpt-4o-mini
writes vague requirements ("needs improvement…"), overclaims ("growing customer concern" from a
single row), and in hybrid mode copied the evidence verbatim into the claim.

**Recommendation:** default to gpt-6-luna in `llm` mode. It needs `reasoning_effort="none"`
on the `chat.completions.create()` call in `llm.py` (otherwise OpenAI rejects tool calls with
a 400) — not in the code yet; the evaluation passed it from a throwaway runner.

## Open problems (for whoever picks this up)

Ordered by impact on the demo. 1–2 decide whether the output looks like prioritized
requirements or a list of one-verbatim paraphrases.

1. **Scoring isn't defined.** `score` takes a free-text `formula` and nothing computes a
   score — 4o-mini's SCR node just restated the requirement, and both hybrid runs paused to ask
   the PM "what scoring criteria?". Needs a real formula (VISION.md: "fixed scoring formula"),
   ideally backend-side. The CSV's `reliability` column (0.72–0.92) is a ready input that no run
   used.
2. **No consolidation — every requirement rests on one row.** Each claim links exactly one
   evidence node. Rows 2, 8 and 11 are all about charging; luna noticed the connection but still
   made a separate claim. Options: prompt rule "if a finding supports an existing claim's theme,
   claim across several evidence_ids", or a two-phase run (extract all evidence, then group).
3. **`quote` field misused outside Evidence.** Requirements and Questions sometimes put the
   model's own text in `quote`, which reads like a citation. Fix: separate `_CONTENT` schemas —
   `quote`/`source_ref` only on `query_data`.
4. **Questions aren't linked to what they ask about.** Both QST-001 nodes have no inputs
   though they ask about REQ-001. Fix: `decide_rule_based()`'s `ask_pm` passes the relevant ids,
   or hybrid lets the LLM fill `inputs`.
5. **Hybrid extracts one finding per file**, because `sources_without_evidence` empties after
   the first `query_data`. Needs a "rows left unprocessed" signal if hybrid should go deeper.
6. **Prompt size grows with the source.** ~2.7k input tokens per call for 12 rows, mostly the
   CSV (`sources` signal in `look()`, marked `shortcut:`). Real verbatim files need chunking or
   per-call row selection before they're seeded.
7. **Unused tools.** No run called `web_search`, `challenge` or `add_assumption` — Look has no
   signal that would trigger them (e.g. "requirement with only one evidence" → `challenge`).
